machine.name: Laboratory jaw crusher of Barrios et al. 2020
machine.source: Table 2, p. 3: feed opening 140 x 90 mm, swing jaw throw 10 mm, stroke frequency 6.0 Hz, closed-side setting 7.5 mm

source.paper: Barrios, Jimenez-Herrera, Fuentes-Torres, Tavares 2020, Minerals 10(8):717, https://doi.org/10.3390/min10080717
source.digitised: validation/digitise_barrios2020.py: pass A 600 dpi marker centroids, pass B 300 dpi bounding-box middles (Fig. 6b: 1200 dpi centroids and 600 dpi extent middles, one marker per class in each of its 30 probability bands); axes calibrated on the plot frame (the axis limits); the two passes differ by the digitisation noise; the digitised figures are package data of crushdem (crushdem/cases/data/barrios2020_digitised.json)

bands.set: Set before any run of the product, in the plan of 2026-10-27 (requirements DM-005): throughput within 10 percent, net power within 30 percent, the reduction ratio F80 over P80 within 15 percent.

ore.name: paper single-particle ore (Barrios et al. 2020 Fig. 6b, pass A, Table 3 contact)
ore.derivation: e_inf_j_kg: fit of E50(d) = E_inf (1 + (d0/d)^phi) through the two coarse single-particle size classes (31.5/26.5 and 63/53 mm, 30 particles each) of Barrios et al. 2020 Fig. 6b (p. 7), pass A, the sample median force of each class mapped with the Table 3 contact; the 16/13.2 class is left out and its misfit reported. d0_m: same fit, phi fixed. phi: assumption: the gneiss value of Tavares 2022 Table 1, fixed (the free three-class fit gives 3.66, see the comment in paper_ore). variance: data value 3.08 = (5/3 sigma_lnF)^2 from the digitised distributions (sigma_lnF 1.05, the mean over the three classes, the 16/13.2 class included); limited to 1.2, the upper end of the range of Tavares 2022 p. 67 (assumption). gamma: assumption: Tavares 2022 p. 69, as in the gneiss stand-in (the paper has no damage model). a_max_percent: assumption: gneiss Santa Luzia, Tavares 2022 Table 4 p. 74 (the paper's progeny is a fixed fit to its jaw product and is not used). b_prime: assumption: same row. emax_ratio: assumption: not tabulated, plain lognormal. force_to_energy: the energy a sphere absorbs at the median breakage force (energy_at_force); a choice, the paper's Fig. 6a contradicts the Table 3 stiffness (contact_check_fig6a). min_diameter_m: assumption: the 63 mm feed over 4 mm is a size ratio of 15.75, inside the 20 of CD-005 (the paper simulated down to 2.36 mm, p. 11).

preset.first_estimate_source: Donovan (2003), section 2.1.3: K1 equal to the closed-side setting, K2 the largest particle of the product, close to the open-side setting, K3 equal to 2.3
preset.ranges_source: King (2000), Technical Notes 5, Crushers, equations 5.8 to 5.10, pages 5-4 and 5-5: the ranges given for standard and short-head Symons cone crushers, used here for a laboratory jaw for want of published jaw values
preset.capacity_model: Sastri (1994), equation 9, W = Vh K1 K2 K3 d, with the factors of equations 2 to 13 on the machine's geometry (the laboratory-jaw module)
preset.ore_link: A times b is 3600 A b' over E50: the equation of the exponents of the two published t10 laws (Narayanan and Whiten 1988; Tavares 2022, https://doi.org/10.14356/kona.2022012, equation 20), which is the product's own algebra and not a published conversion; E50 is that of the particle simulation's ore at the feed class's mean size
preset.power: No work index, A, b or fracture energy of the ore is published, so the population balance predicts no power at these points
